acceptedFindings.title: Prespecified research question and clinical context absent
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a clear question, the analytic choices (variables, model, confounding control) cannot be judged for appropriateness, and the findings lack clinical interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly define the population, intervention/exposure, comparison, outcome, and time frame (PICOT), along with a prespecified analysis plan.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript contains a sentence starting with 'The primary objective was to assess the association between...' with specific variables.

acceptedFindings.title: Unspecified research question
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a clear question (PICO), the analysis lacks direction, and results cannot be interpreted meaningfully or assessed for relevance.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the primary research question, including population, intervention/exposure, comparator, and outcome.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing variable definitions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Interpretation of effect sizes, replication, and clinical relevance depend on understanding variable coding, units, and measurement.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a codebook detailing each variable, its type, coding scheme, and units (e.g., count_events as number of events per patient).

acceptedFindings.title: Poisson model likely misspecified: no offset or exposure variable for count events
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Count outcomes (e.g., number of events per subject) typically require an offset term (log of follow-up time) to model rates correctly. Omitting it biases incidence rate ratios if follow-up varies.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include an offset variable (e.g., log(person-years)) in the Poisson regression, or justify its absence (e.g., all subjects have equal follow-up).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspect the stats-config.json for an offset term; if absent, flag as incomplete.

acceptedFindings.title: No overdispersion assessment or check for zero-inflation
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Poisson regression assumes equidispersion; real-world count data often exhibit overdispersion, leading to underestimated standard errors and inflated type I error. Zero-inflation further biases estimates.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the deviance/df ratio, perform a dispersion test (e.g., dispersiontest in R), and consider negative binomial or zero-inflated models if needed.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check if deviance/df > 1.5; if so, overdispersion likely.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing data handling unreported, complete-case analysis only
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can introduce bias if missingness is related to outcome or covariates. The proportion and pattern of missingness are not disclosed, making results unreliable.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a missing data table, describe the missingness mechanism (MCAR/MAR/MNAR), and conduct sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple imputation).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspect raw data for missingness rates; verify that no additional rows were excluded beyond those already removed.

acceptedFindings.title: No descriptive statistics for study variables
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without summary statistics (Table 1), it is impossible to assess balance, range, outliers, or distribution of count_events, treatment, age, severity, which are essential for model interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a table with n, mean, sd, median, IQR, min/max for continuous variables and counts/frequencies for categorical variables, stratified by exposure if relevant.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of a Table 1 block in the manuscript with the above statistics.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis not fully reproducible due to missing raw data and code
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript mentions only artifact hashes but does not provide the raw dataset, data dictionary, or analysis scripts. This prevents independent verification.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a data availability statement, deposit de-identified data and code in a public repository, or document the exact software environment and seed.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that a 'reproduce.sh' script or README exists in the run directory that regenerates all artifacts from raw data.

acceptedFindings.title: Inadequate Poisson regression diagnostics
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Shapiro–Wilk test on residuals is inappropriate for Poisson models. No overdispersion assessment (e.g., dispersion parameter) or zero-inflation test is performed, risking invalid standard errors and p-values.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute the dispersion statistic (deviance/df) and, if >1, use robust standard errors or a negative binomial model. Test for zero-inflation (e.g., Vuong test) and specify a zero-inflated model if needed.

acceptedFindings.title: No handling of missing data beyond complete-case analysis
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case exclusion can bias results if missingness is related to exposure or outcome; the extent and pattern of missing data are unreported.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number and proportion of missing values per variable, compare baseline characteristics of included vs. excluded records, and consider multiple imputation or sensitivity analyses.

acceptedFindings.title: No analysis code or data preprocessing script provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The analysis cannot be independently verified or rerun without the exact computational steps.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include the complete analysis script (R/Python) with data loading, cleaning, and model fitting, along with a seed for reproducibility.

acceptedFindings.title: No data plausibility checks
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without summary statistics or distributions, impossible values or extreme outliers may distort the model.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide descriptive statistics (mean, median, range) and visualizations (histograms, boxplots) for all variables. Flag any biologically implausible values.

acceptedFindings.title: Overinterpretation given unbound exploratory posture
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The result posture is explicitly exploratory and 'cannot support paper-ready conclusions', yet the manuscript presents p-values and suggests interpretable evidence without adequate caveats.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Downgrade language to explicitly state the exploratory nature, omit p-value interpretations unless a prespecified analysis plan exists, and avoid any implication of clinical actionability.

acceptedFindings.title: Incomplete quality-assurance reporting
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Only 7/9 QA checks passed; the nature of the failures is hidden, undermining confidence in the analysis reliability.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Publish the full stats-qa.json and discuss any failed checks. If failures are trivial, justify; otherwise, rerun analysis with corrections.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Verify that stats-qa.json is complete and its status is not 'warning' at final promotion.

acceptedFindings.title: Exploratory analysis presented as 'local evidence' with p-values
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The result posture explicitly states the analysis is exploratory and cannot support 'paper-ready conclusions'. Yet the manuscript frames p-values and estimates as 'local evidence', risking overinterpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Downgrade the language to 'exploratory findings only' and remove p-values or clearly label them as unadjusted, hypothesis-generating.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the Discussion begins with a statement matching the resultPosture label.

acceptedFindings.title: No literature contextualization
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Scientific contribution and interpretation require comparison with existing evidence.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review, citing prior studies on similar exposures/outcomes, and compare direction and magnitude of effects.

reviewAdjudication.nextAction: Route back to protocol with review-response decisions.
